summary: I traced solution/triage.py (installed by solve.sh) against every rule in case-guide.md, record-formats.md and report.md, covering the normal case, the boundaries and the interactions within the stated input domain. I found no concrete incorrect behaviour: clock-step correction in both directions, year rollover, btmp-based hostility with the 600 s bound inclusive, wtmp initial access, the address/key/terminal fixed point, privilege escalation, persistence with the inclusive 2 s package exclusion, and first/last activity that excludes collected_utc all match the contract.

unread_or_truncated_ranges: environment/app/evidence/case-1/var/log/auth.log.2.gz, auth.log.3.gz and btmp: gzip or binary files that I treated as opaque (no shell to decode them). wtmp rendered only partially as text. These are case-1 development samples, not contract authorities. I judged the reference's parsing of them against the record formats in record-formats.md:28-34 and model.py:470-563.

checks_performed: Confirmed that solve.sh copies solution/triage.py to /app/triage.py. The installed program uses only the standard library, imports nothing from model.py, seal.py or /app/evidence, and only reads the evidence directory.
Traced read_collection and date_lines: offset sign, collected_utc parsing, year taken from the collection-local time, and one year subtracted when walking back from a later month (Dec->Jan crossing).

Traced the clock-step detection (solution/triage.py:114-135) for a forward step (N>0) and a backward step (N<0). Collector copies are keyed by the pid-bearing sshd message. step_n is the host-to-collector difference and step_t/step_i is the first matching line after the mismatch. Auth-log lines are corrected by file position; other host-clock readings are corrected when their host time is below step_t.

Checked the backward-step overlap: record-formats says auth lines arrive in true order, and model.py:402-427 places the step so that no graded record falls where host times overlap. Every pre-step record therefore has a host time below tc and every post-step record a host time of at least tc+n.

Traced hostility over btmp type-6 records after fix(): ts[i+4]-ts[i] <= 600, so exactly 600 s is inclusive. Checked the 'brute' family at exactly 600 s, the carol/ivan decoy whose five attempts span more than 600 s, O2 mistypes (at most 4) and scanners that never log in.
Traced initial access: the earliest wtmp type-7 session from a hostile address, using the corrected time.

Traced the rule 4 fixed point. Keys are extracted from the histories of intruder accounts, only from commands mentioning authorized_keys (both the '>> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys' and '| sudo tee -a /root/.ssh/authorized_keys' forms). Fingerprints are computed as record-formats.md:44-45 specifies, and a matching Accepted publickey adds the address. Legitimate same-account password logins from other addresses are not tied.

Traced the sudo terminal tie via session_at(tty, t): the tty must belong to a wtmp session that contains the sudo time. Verified that tty allocation in model.py:481-487 never reuses a pts while it is busy, so ties are unambiguous. Legitimate victim and admin sudos on other ttys during the attack are excluded.

Traced privilege escalation: min over tied sudo-to-root lines and intruder root logins (both the rootlogin family and a root key login). The result is null when neither exists, and root is added to accounts when escalation exists.

Traced persistence: path-kind predicate (cron.d, crontabs, systemd .service/.timer including the wants/ symlinks, rc.local, root/home authorized_keys) plus corrected ctime inside an intruder session window. Package exclusion uses the corrected dpkg 'status installed' time and the .list membership with |delta| <= 2 inclusive, which covers the edge_lo/edge_hi ±2 s cases. The certbot-renew decoy (ctime between windows, old mtime inside the window) is excluded, and a touch -r forged mtime is still caught through ctime.

Traced first and last activity: btmp failures from intruder addresses (including failures days earlier), intruder wtmp logins and logouts, tied sudo lines, persistence ctimes, and stamped intruder-account history inside intruder windows after fix(). An open session contributes no end and collected_utc is not an event.
Checked the output shape against report.md: exactly seven keys, lists deduplicated and sorted, privilege_escalation null or ISO time, and every time formatted as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.
Checked that the program tolerates optional directories being absent (home, root, dpkg info, remote; missing wtmp/btmp/dpkg.log) as record-formats.md:3-4 allows.

Sanity-checked case-1 statically: remote log attacker login git@77.157.180.252 at 2021-12-29T16:39:40Z, an overlapping legitimate git login from 10.233.9.93 on pts/1, a later key login from 193.3.49.175 with the key echoed in git's history, and root history stamps about 1.5 h behind (a forward step within 30-7200 s) that fix() is designed to correct.

coverage_sweep.category: Trace an ordinary case and each relevant boundary through the reference logic
coverage_sweep.reason: Traced ordinary and boundary cases for rules 1-7: the 600 s window at exactly 600, package ctime delta of exactly 2, a Dec->Jan year crossing, offsets -12:00 and +14:00, 1 or 6 auth files with rotation, clock steps of 30 and 7200 s forward and backward, an open final session, and no escalation.

coverage_sweep.category: Output bytes: widths, precision, delimiters, paths
coverage_sweep.reason: iso() emits %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ in UTC. The JSON has exactly the report.md keys. List fields are deduplicated by sets and dicts. Persistence entries are absolute host paths taken from fs-listing.

coverage_sweep.category: State-updating branches (loop state, identifier reuse, replacement)
coverage_sweep.reason: Checked wtmp login/logout pairing through open_by_line (a logout pops the latest login on that line). The fixed-point loop recomputes esc/pe each iteration from monotonically growing sets and terminates on no change. Collector matching keys are pid-bearing sshd messages that are unique per session.

coverage_sweep.category: Recovery and durability claims at interruption points
coverage_sweep.reason: The task is a single-pass read-only analyzer that writes one JSON file. It makes no recovery or durability promises.

coverage_sweep.category: Environment constraints (stdlib only, unprivileged, read-only evidence, no dependency on /app/evidence)
coverage_sweep.reason: Imports are stdlib only. The program only reads the evidence and writes the output path argument. solve.sh installs a single file.

interaction_sweep.case_or_path: The dpkg status-installed time and the file ctime both lie on the host clock and both pass through fix(), so the 2 s comparison is made in true time. For a backward step, model.py overlap_is_empty keeps the dpkg and ctime records out of the ambiguous band.

btmp and wtmp times are corrected before the 600 s window and the earliest-login ordering are applied. The step lies at or after t_ia+60, so the attacker's failures sit uniformly on the pre-step side.

A root-shell attacker writes the key into /root/.ssh/authorized_keys from root's history. root enters accounts only after pe is found, and the fixed point then reads root's history, finds the key and adds B through Accepted publickey. A root key login from B also counts toward pe.

In the 'sudo' family, a legitimate victim session from O2 and an admin session run sudo between t_ia and t_pe. session_at maps each sudo to the session on its tty, so only sudos on intruder ttys count toward pe and activity.

rules: files whose mtime differs from ctime
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: The touch -r forged file (old mtime, ctime t+2) is included through ctime. The certbot-renew decoy (mtime inside window 0, ctime between windows) is excluded.
A final intruder session with no logout extends its window to collected_utc for persistence and history membership, but contributes no end event.

Files are read highest rotation first. The year is anchored on the last line against the collection-local time and decremented on backward month transitions (Dec->Jan). A backward step is placed within one month.
